candidates.rule: Build PR bodies from the checked-in .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md rather than a hardcoded copy, and preserve the template's instructional HTML comments and mandated section text instead of stripping all comments.
candidates.trigger: Agent instructions, tooling, or docs that generate a PR body embed their own copy of the template, or instruct that all HTML comments be removed from the template.

candidates.rule: Keep types-* stub packages excluded from automated dependency bumps; their version must be pinned to match the installed version of the upstream runtime dependency they type.
candidates.trigger: A renovate/dependabot config adds or removes a types-* entry from the ignore/exclude list, or a types-* pin is bumped without a matching bump of its upstream package.

candidates.rule: A coordinator's _async_update_data must not issue one sequential API request per device; use the library's batch endpoint, or at minimum asyncio.gather, so the polling interval does not multiply request volume by device count.
candidates.trigger: _async_update_data contains a for-loop over devices with an awaited per-device API call inside it, following an initial list/devices call.

candidates.rule: Keep device- and API-specific data marshalling (timestamp formatting, parameter string construction) in the upstream vendor library rather than in the integration's coordinator.
candidates.trigger: A coordinator or entity module defines helpers that format datetimes or build vendor-specific request parameter strings before passing them to the library client.

candidates.rule: Adding an entity platform module, or a new entity description to an existing platform's descriptions tuple, requires accompanying tests covering entity creation and state - with snapshot assertions for entity attributes.
candidates.trigger: A diff adds homeassistant/components/<domain>/<platform>.py or appends an EntityDescription with a new key/device_class, without a matching added or extended tests/components/<domain>/test_<platform>.py.

candidates.rule: Key entity caches and lookup dictionaries by a stable unique identifier (the entity's unique_id), never by its display name.
candidates.trigger: A module stores entities in a dict keyed by a human-readable name variable (sensor_name, friendly name, topic label) and later checks `if key not in store` to decide between creating and updating.

candidates.rule: User-facing strings in strings.json must follow Home Assistant string style: spell out "for example" instead of "e.g.", avoid slash constructions such as "Folder/Prefix", and wrap literal example values in backticks rather than quotes.
candidates.trigger: An added or changed value in strings.json (name, description, data_description) contains a slash-joined noun pair, "e.g.", or an example value in single/double quotes.

candidates.rule: Log per-item skip or parse failures at debug level; reserve _LOGGER.warning for conditions the user can act on and that cannot repeat once per listed item.
candidates.trigger: A _LOGGER.warning call sits inside a loop over remote objects/files in an except branch that merely skips the item.

candidates.rule: A failing backup agent must fail only itself: an exception raised by one backup platform must not abort the overall backup or the other platforms, and the platform API contract is documented rather than defensively re-validated.
candidates.trigger: Changes to the backup agent/platform API (agent.py, manager.py) that propagate a single agent's exception into the shared backup flow, or add per-call validation of platform-supplied callbacks.

candidates.rule: Do not silence an untyped third-party return value with a broad `# type: ignore`; cast the value explicitly (e.g. int(...)) or add typing for the library function.
candidates.trigger: A return statement or assignment gains a `# type: ignore[no-any-return]` (or similar blanket ignore) around a call into an untyped external dependency.

candidates.rule: An entity lifecycle override must call the matching base-class hook (async_will_remove_from_hass calls super().async_will_remove_from_hass()); never satisfy the home-assistant-missing-super-call check by calling a different hook or by disabling it.
candidates.trigger: An overridden async_added_to_hass / async_will_remove_from_hass calls a super() method with a different name, or adds `# pylint: disable-next=home-assistant-missing-super-call`.

candidates.rule: Guard CI jobs that consume repository secrets so they are skipped, not failed, when the secret is unavailable - notably on pull_request runs from forks.
candidates.trigger: A workflow step or job references secrets.* (or validates a token via a validate_*_secret script) without an if: condition on the secret being present or on the event not being a fork pull_request.

candidates.rule: Write all code comments, docstrings and identifiers in English; non-English comments must be translated before merge.
candidates.trigger: An added line inside homeassistant/components/ contains a comment or docstring with non-ASCII, non-English text (e.g. CJK characters).

candidates.rule: Every rule status in an integration's quality_scale.yaml must reflect what the code actually implements; do not leave a rule as todo when the corresponding implementation is already present.
candidates.trigger: A quality_scale.yaml adds or keeps a rule marked todo/exempt while the integration source already contains the implementation for that rule (e.g. config-entry-unloading: todo alongside async_unload_entry in __init__.py).

candidates.rule: Normalize MAC addresses with homeassistant.helpers.device_registry.format_mac before using them as a config entry unique ID or device identifier; never hand-roll uppercasing/colon insertion.
candidates.trigger: A config flow or entity builds a MAC string via .upper(), .lower(), string slicing or ":".join(...) and passes it to async_set_unique_id or device identifiers.

candidates.rule: A service handler must only index call.data with keys declared in that specific service's voluptuous schema; for optional or per-service fields use call.data.get() and handle the missing case.
candidates.trigger: A shared service handler branches on an attribute constant and reads call.data[ATTR_X] where ATTR_X is not part of the schema registered for the service being executed.

candidates.rule: Authentication failures that start a reauth flow must surface a distinct user-facing message stating that reauthentication is required, and must not interpolate the raw exception text into it.
candidates.trigger: An except clause groups an authentication error with connection/transport errors into one HomeAssistantError whose message is generic or embeds f"...{err}".

candidates.rule: Gate conditional entity creation on the capability flag or coordinator data key that actually supplies the entity's value, not on an unrelated module/feature flag.
candidates.trigger: An entity is appended inside an if that tests a capability key different from the datapoint key the entity description reads (e.g. entity keyed on hidro.* created only when main.hasCL is set).

candidates.rule: When the user step and the reauth step of a config flow perform the same validation, share one implementation and branch on the flow type at the end rather than duplicating the connect/validate block.
candidates.trigger: config_flow.py contains async_step_reauth_confirm whose try/except validation body duplicates async_step_user, differing only in the final async_create_entry vs async_update_reload_and_abort.

candidates.rule: Derive per-config-entry values once in the integration's async_setup_entry and expose them through entry.runtime_data, rather than re-deriving them (with repeated asserts) in every platform module.
candidates.trigger: The same block fetching a client/session attribute plus assert statements to narrow it appears in two or more platform modules (binary_sensor.py, sensor.py, switch.py, cover.py) of one integration.

candidates.rule: Call _abort_if_unique_id_mismatch with an explicit reason= argument that matches an abort key in strings.json instead of relying on the default reason.
candidates.trigger: A reconfigure or reauth config-flow step calls self._abort_if_unique_id_mismatch() with no arguments.

candidates.rule: Reference existing translation keys with the [%key:...%] reference syntax in strings.json instead of repeating the same label or data_description text in a second step.
candidates.trigger: A strings.json diff adds a data/data_description value that is textually identical to one already present under another step in the same file.

candidates.rule: Adding an authorization decorator such as @require_admin to an HTTP view requires a regression test asserting a non-admin user is rejected, not just the existing happy-path admin test.
candidates.trigger: A diff adds @require_admin (or another auth guard) to an aiohttp view handler in homeassistant/components/*/http_api.py or http.py.

candidates.rule: Create entities only for the parameters/features actually present on the specific device instance, rather than iterating the full static device-definition table in async_setup_entry.
candidates.trigger: async_setup_entry loops over a module-level DEVICE_DEFINITIONS/PARAMS constant and appends an entity per entry without checking the device's reported state or capability list.

candidates.rule: Keep the fields exposed in a domain's triggers.yaml in sync with what the underlying trigger schema accepts, including the common `for` duration field.
candidates.trigger: A triggers.yaml diff removes or omits a field (such as `for` with a duration selector) that the entity trigger schema for that domain still supports.

candidates.rule: The diagnostics TO_REDACT set must list every identifying field actually stored in the config entry, including MAC addresses and device identifiers, not only credentials.
candidates.trigger: A diagnostics.py defines TO_REDACT/TO_REDACT_ENTRY covering API keys, hosts and passwords while the integration's config entry data or tests also contain a MAC/serial key.

candidates.rule: Selector options presented in a config flow must carry a user-facing, translatable label instead of reusing the raw internal option value.
candidates.trigger: A config flow builds SelectOptionDict(value=X, label=X) or otherwise passes an internal constant straight through as the displayed label.

candidates.rule: HomeAssistantError raised from an entity service handler must name the rejected value and, where a fixed set exists, the accepted values.
candidates.trigger: An entity service method raises HomeAssistantError with a bare static message such as `Invalid source` after a lookup against a mapping constant returns None.

candidates.rule: Clamp incoming entity-service values to their documented Home Assistant range before converting them into device units.
candidates.trigger: async_set_volume_level (or a similar service handler) multiplies the incoming 0..1 float by a device range and offset without bounding it first.

candidates.rule: Interpret values returned by an integration's pinned library in the units that library version documents and tests, and validate ranges in those same units.
candidates.trigger: Integration code applies a magic divisor or threshold to a raw value from the third-party library (for example dividing a tuner frequency by 100 and comparing against a hard-coded maximum).

candidates.rule: When platform setup branches between the legacy and non-legacy path, add test coverage for the non-legacy branch that routes to EntityComponent.async_setup_platform, not only the legacy one.
candidates.trigger: A diff changes discovery or platform-loading code that checks platform.type != PLATFORM_TYPE_LEGACY and delegates to component.async_setup_platform.

candidates.rule: Config flow connection helpers must catch the same exception set the integration already handles during entry setup, including TimeoutError, not just the library's own error base class.
candidates.trigger: A config-flow helper awaits a device/library call inside `except <Lib>Error:` while __init__.py or the coordinator for the same integration also catches TimeoutError around the equivalent call.

candidates.rule: Do not override a @final base-entity property and silence the error with type: ignore; add an explicit extension hook to the base class instead.
candidates.trigger: An in-tree entity subclass redefines a property that the base class marks @final, accompanied by `# type: ignore[misc]`.

candidates.rule: Fetch per-device or per-sub-unit data concurrently inside a DataUpdateCoordinator refresh instead of awaiting the calls in a for loop.
candidates.trigger: A coordinator's _async_update_data awaits a client call inside a `for` loop over circuits/zones/devices and assembles the results into a dict.

candidates.rule: Map device value ranges onto Home Assistant ranges with the existing shared range/percentage helpers used by fan and light platforms instead of hand-rolling a conversion table in const.py.
candidates.trigger: A new integration defines its own dict comprehension or arithmetic constant mapping device steps onto the 1-255 brightness range or a 0-100 percentage.

candidates.rule: Populate every entity _attr_* value from the device in a single shared method called from both __init__ and the state-update callback, so no attribute is left unset until the first push update.
candidates.trigger: An entity __init__ assigns a subset of _attr_* values from the device while a separate _async_handle_state_update or _handle_coordinator_update assigns a different, larger set.

candidates.rule: Do not optimistically assign _attr_is_on (or similar state) and call async_write_ha_state after issuing a device command when the device library already reports the new state through a callback.
candidates.trigger: async_turn_on/async_turn_off sends a command and then sets _attr_* and calls self.async_write_ha_state() in an integration that registers a device state callback.

candidates.rule: Give every new entity an _attr_translation_key and a matching entry in strings.json, following the entity translation pattern the integration's other platforms already use.
candidates.trigger: A new entity class sets _attr_device_class or _attr_name without an _attr_translation_key, in an integration whose other platforms define translation keys.

candidates.rule: Thread the ConfigEntry explicitly through discovery callbacks that run off the event loop rather than looking entries up from hass inside those callbacks.
candidates.trigger: A discovery helper or zeroconf/mDNS callback executing on a non-event-loop thread reaches into hass to find a config entry or its runtime_data.

candidates.rule: In quality_scale.yaml, mark rules that cannot apply to the integration as exempt with a short comment explaining why, instead of leaving them as todo.
candidates.trigger: A quality_scale.yaml adds or keeps `todo` for a rule (reauthentication-flow, parallel-updates, discovery, etc.) that the integration structurally cannot satisfy.

candidates.rule: Reset every entity attribute that is only computed on one branch of a state update on all the sibling branches too, so an entity never reports values left over from a previous update cycle.
candidates.trigger: An entity's async_update/state-derivation method assigns a private attribute (e.g. self._in_zones) inside one conditional branch but leaves it untouched in the elif/else branches.

candidates.rule: Create shared clients and connections once during async_setup_entry, store them on entry.runtime_data, and close them in async_unload_entry; entities must consume that object rather than constructing their own instance.
candidates.trigger: An entity __init__ or helper method instantiates a client/session/resolver of the same type that the integration's __init__.py already creates and stores on entry.runtime_data.

candidates.rule: User-facing text in strings.json must be sentence-cased; only the literal product/brand name keeps its capitalization, and any common noun appended to it is lowercased.
candidates.trigger: A new title, name or description in strings.json capitalizes a common noun mid-sentence (e.g. "Connect to EARN-E P1 Meter").

candidates.rule: The field keys under services.<service>.fields in strings.json must correspond exactly to the fields that service declares in services.yaml - add to both files or neither.
candidates.trigger: strings.json adds (or keeps) a field entry under one service while that service's block in services.yaml has no matching field key.

candidates.rule: Default polling intervals for local-polling integrations belong in the 30-60 second range; a SCAN_INTERVAL or update_interval under roughly 30 seconds must be justified or made configurable.
candidates.trigger: A coordinator module sets SCAN_INTERVAL or DataUpdateCoordinator(update_interval=...) to a timedelta below about 30 seconds.

candidates.rule: Set suggested_display_precision explicitly on sensor entity descriptions instead of relying on the device-class default.
candidates.trigger: A new SensorEntityDescription declares device_class/state_class (and snapshot tests show a rounded value) but omits suggested_display_precision.

candidates.rule: When a trigger platform is adapted from another domain, rewrite its comments and stated rationale to describe the new domain's entities rather than the domain it was copied from.
candidates.trigger: A new homeassistant/components/<domain>/trigger.py contains comments naming a different domain's entity (e.g. "the first time the button is pressed" inside the event trigger).

candidates.rule: A config flow that holds a live device connection must clear the client reference right after an explicit disconnect on the success path, so the flow's finally block or async_remove does not disconnect a second time.
candidates.trigger: A config_flow step calls await self._client.disconnect()/close() before async_create_entry while a finally block or async_remove also tears down self._client.

candidates.rule: Subentry reconfigure flows must schedule the parent entry reload explicitly rather than depending on the config entry update listener, which does not exist while the entry is unloaded or in SETUP_RETRY.
candidates.trigger: A subentry flow calls async_update_and_abort (or async_update_entry) and relies on an update listener registered in async_setup_entry to apply the change.

candidates.rule: Filter config_entry.subentries by subentry_type before counting or iterating them; never treat the whole subentries mapping as one type.
candidates.trigger: Code uses len(self.config_entry.subentries) or iterates config_entry.subentries.values() without comparing subentry.subentry_type against the expected type constant.

candidates.rule: Value helpers called during a coordinator refresh must return None for missing or empty device data instead of raising; only genuine failures may propagate as UpdateFailed.
candidates.trigger: A value_fn or state helper indexes a library result (list[0], dict[key]) inside the coordinator update path while catching only transport exceptions such as RequestException.

candidates.rule: Do not call hass.async_add_executor_job once per item inside a loop or comprehension; collect the blocking work into a single function and schedule that on the executor one time.
candidates.trigger: await hass.async_add_executor_job(...) appears inside a for-loop, list comprehension, or the condition of a comprehension over entity descriptions.

candidates.rule: Trigger transition predicates for cover-backed domains must account for the opening and closing states explicitly, because a cover reports those states before is_closed is consulted and is_closed may still be None then.
candidates.trigger: An is_valid_transition (or similar) in a domain trigger.py compares ATTR_IS_CLOSED between from_state and to_state for COVER_DOMAIN entities without handling STATE_OPENING/STATE_CLOSING or a None is_closed.

candidates.rule: Refactoring a trigger's triggers.yaml field schema must preserve every field the previous schema exposed (notably the `for` duration field); removing one is a breaking change for existing automations.
candidates.trigger: A diff to triggers.yaml or a trigger field schema deletes or renames existing field keys instead of only adding new ones.

candidates.rule: A dhcp discovery block in manifest.json that matches on hostname should also declare registered_devices so devices already in the device registry are still matched by MAC when their hostname differs.
candidates.trigger: manifest.json gains a `dhcp` array whose entries only contain hostname or macaddress matchers, with no registered_devices flag.

candidates.rule: Compose _attr_unique_id from every identifier that can vary inside one config entry - include the device/node id alongside the config entry unique id and the entity description key.
candidates.trigger: _attr_unique_id is an f-string of only coordinator.config_entry.unique_id and description.key while the entity class is instantiated per device/node returned by the API.

candidates.rule: Every rule marked `done` in quality_scale.yaml must be backed by the code actually present in the integration; mark it todo or exempt (with a comment) when the implementation is missing.
candidates.trigger: quality_scale.yaml declares a rule as done (e.g. `devices: done`) while the corresponding implementation - DeviceInfo on the entity, a reauth flow, tests - is absent from the diff.

candidates.rule: Device registry migrations must build properly typed set[tuple[str, str]] identifier sets (filtering out legacy shapes) instead of silencing the mismatch with `# type: ignore` on identifiers or async_update_device.
candidates.trigger: A migration helper adds `# type: ignore[comparison-overlap]` or `# type: ignore[arg-type]` around device_entry.identifiers or async_update_device(new_identifiers=...).

candidates.rule: async_unload_entry must await async_unload_platforms first and only stop or close runtime resources when that call returned True, returning the same value.
candidates.trigger: async_unload_entry awaits a stop/close/disconnect on entry.runtime_data before calling async_unload_platforms, or ignores the boolean it returns.

candidates.rule: Log messages must not repeat the integration name, brand or domain - the logger prefix already carries it.
candidates.trigger: A _LOGGER.debug/info/warning/error message string contains the integration's brand or domain name (e.g. "EARN-E P1 UDP listener stopped").

candidates.rule: An exception translation key in strings.json must describe only the failure it is raised for; when one key is reused for several distinct exception types, either broaden the message to cover all of them or split it into separate keys.
candidates.trigger: A new key under the "exceptions" block of strings.json whose message names one specific failure mode, while the matching raise site in coordinator.py/__init__.py uses that translation_key for more than one exception class.

candidates.rule: Values assigned to context["title_placeholders"] in a discovery config-flow step must not repeat punctuation already supplied by the flow_title template; add a separate placeholder rather than embedding a parenthesised name inside {name}.
candidates.trigger: A discovery step (bluetooth/zeroconf/dhcp) sets self.context["title_placeholders"] to an f-string containing parentheses while strings.json defines flow_title as "{name} ({address})".

candidates.rule: system_health_info must never raise on unexpected API payload types: coerce values fetched from Supervisor or another external API before formatting them and skip the field on ValueError/TypeError.
candidates.trigger: system_health.py applies a numeric format spec (f"{value:.0f}", arithmetic, rounding) directly to a value read out of an external info dict with .get().

candidates.rule: A fan async_turn_on must always leave the fan running: treat percentage == 0 as if no percentage were supplied and fall through to the default speed instead of mapping it to the off mode.
candidates.trigger: async_turn_on branches on `percentage is not None` and forwards the value to async_set_percentage, which maps 0 to an OFF mode.

candidates.rule: CoordinatorEntity properties and EntityDescription value_fn callbacks must handle coordinator.data being None, returning None rather than dereferencing it unconditionally.
candidates.trigger: A native_value/is_on/available property calls self.entity_description.value_fn(self.coordinator.data) or attribute-accesses self.coordinator.data without a None guard, while value_fn is typed for the non-optional data class.

candidates.rule: Use Core and Supervisor terminology precisely in docstrings and user-facing text: a repair is a Core concept, while the Supervisor raises an issue and a suggestion; do not attribute a repair to the Supervisor.
candidates.trigger: A docstring, comment, log line or string says the Supervisor raises/creates a repair, or otherwise mixes Core repair vocabulary with Supervisor issue/suggestion vocabulary.

candidates.rule: Brand names in strings.json must be capitalised consistently across every message in the integration; when a PR adds strings using a different capitalisation than the existing ones, normalise them in the same PR.
candidates.trigger: New entries in strings.json spell the brand differently from neighbouring pre-existing entries in the same file (for example Homee alongside homee).

candidates.rule: A unique-id migration map must supply every field the migration helper needs for each legacy class, including an explicit channel for single-channel devices, so no entry causes the helper to return None and leave entities unmigrated.
candidates.trigger: Entries are added to a UNIQUE_ID_MIGRATION_MAP (or similar) omitting a field that the _migrate_unique_id helper requires to build the new unique id, so the helper's fallback returns None.

candidates.rule: A light async_turn_on must preserve the current brightness when the call supplies only other attributes such as effect or hs_color; default to full brightness only for a bare turn-on with no attributes.
candidates.trigger: async_turn_on initialises brightness to a constant (for example 255) and overwrites it only when ATTR_BRIGHTNESS is present in kwargs.

candidates.rule: Optional values must be omitted from config entry data rather than stored as None; build the data dict conditionally instead of always writing the key.
candidates.trigger: async_create_entry (or async_update_entry) passes a data dict that always includes an optional key such as CONF_PASSWORD whose value may be None.

candidates.rule: Helpers in const.py (or any integration module) that are imported by other modules or by the tests must be given public names; do not export underscore-prefixed functions across module boundaries.
candidates.trigger: A new `def _name(...)` in const.py or a shared module is imported from coordinator.py, an entity platform, or tests/.

candidates.rule: State flags that gate issue-registry calls must be initialised to their real starting value (False), not None, so the first coordinator refresh does not treat the initial state as a transition and call async_delete_issue for an issue that was never created.
candidates.trigger: A coordinator declares a tracking attribute as `bool | None = None` and compares it against the freshly computed boolean to decide between async_create_issue and async_delete_issue.

candidates.rule: A config flow must validate the connection by calling the same third-party library client the coordinator uses; it must not re-implement API paths, endpoints or response parsing inline.
candidates.trigger: config_flow.py builds a URL path, issues aiohttp/requests calls or parses the API JSON payload itself instead of instantiating the integration's client class and calling its method.

candidates.rule: manifest.json must list only keys the integration actually uses; empty placeholder keys such as "requirements": [], "ssdp": [], "zeroconf": [], "homekit" or "dependencies" must be deleted rather than left empty.
candidates.trigger: A new or edited manifest.json contains a key whose value is an empty list or empty object.

candidates.rule: Integration API wrappers must not add their own HTTP status-code branches for 4xx, 429 or 5xx responses when the shared Home Assistant helper layer already maps those responses onto ConfigEntryAuthFailed / ConfigEntryNotReady.
candidates.trigger: api.py or a session/auth helper inspects ex.status ranges (400 <= status < 500, TOO_MANY_REQUESTS, 5xx) on a ClientResponseError and raises a config-entry exception that the framework already raises.

candidates.rule: Set entity translation keys through _attr_translation_key or an EntityDescription; never assign a bare class attribute named translation_key on an entity class.
candidates.trigger: An entity class body contains `translation_key = "..."` without the `_attr_` prefix and outside an EntityDescription.

candidates.rule: async_get_config_entry_diagnostics must expose the runtime coordinator data (redacted), not just the redacted config entry, when the integration claims the diagnostics quality-scale rule.
candidates.trigger: A new diagnostics.py returns only async_redact_data({"config_entry": config_entry.as_dict()}, TO_REDACT) while quality_scale.yaml marks diagnostics as done and runtime_data holds coordinator state.

candidates.rule: The PR description must match what the diff actually does; when a described removal or added payload is not carried out (a compatibility shim keeps the field, or diagnostics omit the promised data), either change the code or correct the description and any quality-scale claim before merge.
candidates.trigger: A PR description announces removing a key from hass.data, adding data to a payload, or satisfying a quality-scale rule, but the diff keeps the key via a compatibility layer or omits the payload.

candidates.rule: When a coroutine is converted to a plain def helper, its docstring must stop describing it as a coroutine.
candidates.trigger: A diff changes `async def` to `def` (or adds a `def` helper) whose docstring still begins with wording such as "Init coroutine to ..." and the body never awaits.

candidates.rule: A targeted refresh path that updates one object's state must also update every shared hass.data key derived from it that other coordinators read, not only the coordinator's own data.
candidates.trigger: A force/partial refresh helper writes to a coordinator's own data or a single DATA_* key while another coordinator in the same integration keys its work off a different DATA_* list that the helper leaves stale.

candidates.rule: Do not add another per-refresh client call inside a coordinator's `_async_update_data`; obtain the extra field from the existing bulk call, bundle the requests, or document the added request cost.
candidates.trigger: A diff adds a new `await self.client.<something>()` line inside `_async_update_data` alongside existing client calls.

candidates.rule: Entity properties must not assume `self.coordinator.data` is populated; check `is not None` before dereferencing it and return `None`/unavailable otherwise.
candidates.trigger: An entity property or `available` override dereferences `self.coordinator.data.<attr>` with no `is not None` guard.

candidates.rule: Do not re-scan `hass.config_entries` for an entry that a helper on the same code path already resolved; return the entry from that helper or call `async_entry_for_domain_unique_id` once.
candidates.trigger: A `for entry in self._get_config_entries()` loop or a repeated `async_entry_for_domain_unique_id` call following a helper that already looked the same entry up.

candidates.rule: Never suppress `asyncio.CancelledError` around long-lived awaits in a coordinator; catch it explicitly, cancel/await the pending future, and re-raise when the current task is genuinely being cancelled.
candidates.trigger: `with suppress(..., asyncio.CancelledError, ...)` or `except asyncio.CancelledError: pass` wrapping an awaited IDLE/long-poll future.

candidates.rule: Integrations must not read private attributes of Home Assistant core helper objects; use a public API, or document why none exists and what upstream change would break the access.
candidates.trigger: An underscore-prefixed attribute access on a core object (e.g. `self.stream._thread`), typically marked with `# noqa: SLF001`.

candidates.rule: A sensor whose value can be a non-numeric enum state must not unconditionally declare a numeric state class; make the state class conditional on the numeric variant or model the numeric and enum representations separately.
candidates.trigger: A state-class mapping or entity description assigning `SensorStateClass.MEASUREMENT`/`TOTAL*` to a key for which `strings.json` also defines enum `state` values.

candidates.rule: Do device registration and stale-device cleanup once in the coordinator's `_async_setup`, not in `_async_update_data`.
candidates.trigger: Device registry writes or `async_cleanup_stale_devices(...)` called from `_async_update_data`.

candidates.rule: Do not call `_LOGGER.exception` for expected communication failures inside `_async_update_data`; log a warning with the error message or let the coordinator report the failure.
candidates.trigger: `_LOGGER.exception(...)` in an except block of a coordinator update method handling connection/HTTP errors.

candidates.rule: Config flow steps must catch the client library's connection, timeout and authentication exceptions and map them to specific abort reasons or `errors` keys (`cannot_connect`, `invalid_auth`, `not_found`) rather than raising or falling back to `unknown`.
candidates.trigger: A `config_flow.py` step (including DHCP/discovery steps) that calls the library with no except clause, or whose only handling maps every failure to `reason="unknown"`.

candidates.rule: Entity names in `strings.json` must read as a natural sentence-cased phrase rather than a prefixed label with a colon, and related keys should share a common suffix instead of a common prefix.
candidates.trigger: New `entity.<platform>.<key>.name` entries whose values share a leading word plus colon, or whose keys share a leading token such as `alarm_`.

candidates.rule: Do not splat a remote payload dict into an event entity's attributes; nest it under a dedicated `data` key so payload keys cannot overwrite reserved attributes.
candidates.trigger: `self._trigger_event(...)` (or event attribute construction) that merges `**data.get("data", {})` into the top-level attribute dict.

candidates.rule: A dependency version-bump PR must not carry `fixes #<issue>` references for feature requests that the bump does not actually implement.
candidates.trigger: A diff touching only a `manifest.json` `requirements` pin while the PR description contains issue-closing keywords.

candidates.rule: Do not set `_attr_translation_key` on an entity whose device class already yields the correct default name; rely on the device-class default translation instead.
candidates.trigger: A new entity class that sets `_attr_device_class` together with a `_attr_translation_key` whose meaning merely restates that device class.

candidates.rule: Schedule integration background work with `entry.async_create_background_task`/`entry.async_create_task` rather than `hass.async_create_task`, so the task is tracked and cancelled when the config entry unloads.
candidates.trigger: `hass.async_create_task(` called from integration setup, a coordinator listener, or any entry-scoped callback.

candidates.rule: When interpolating a caught exception into a `ConfigEntryNotReady` message, fall back to the exception type name so exceptions with an empty `str()` do not produce a blank setup-failure message.
candidates.trigger: `raise ConfigEntryNotReady(f"...: {exc}")` where the except clause catches `TimeoutError` or other exceptions that stringify to an empty value.

candidates.rule: `quality_scale.yaml` statuses must match what the integration actually implements; mark a rule `todo` (or `exempt` with a comment) rather than `done` when the corresponding code is missing.
candidates.trigger: A `quality_scale.yaml` diff marking a rule `done` with no matching implementation in the integration, e.g. `reauthentication-flow: done` without an `async_step_reauth` in `config_flow.py`.

candidates.rule: Media source identifier parsing must validate the identifier before assigning its parts and raise a translated `Unresolvable`/`BrowseError`; a malformed or empty identifier must never surface as an `UnboundLocalError` or `AttributeError`.
candidates.trigger: A `from_identifier`/`async_resolve_media` implementation that splits an identifier and assigns fields inside a loop without checking that any parts exist.

candidates.rule: Map raw device values to Home Assistant states using enum members exposed by the integration's library rather than magic integers embedded in an entity description.
candidates.trigger: An entity description literal contains a state/value mapping keyed by bare integers (e.g. `state_mapping={1000: "standby", 1001: "charging"}`) instead of library enum members.

candidates.rule: Tests must exercise every value declared in an entity description's state mapping, not just the value present in the default fixture.
candidates.trigger: A diff adds or extends a `state_mapping`/options dict on an entity description while the accompanying tests only assert the fixture's default value.

candidates.rule: Do not name a variable `platform` when it holds an entity domain such as `switch` or `select`; call it `domain`/`entity_domain` and keep `platform` for the Home Assistant platform concept.
candidates.trigger: A loop or parameter named `platform` is assigned entity-domain strings and passed to registry helpers such as entity-unique-id lookups.

candidates.rule: An entity's state property must read the same field the command method writes; after a successful command, update the entity's own state optimistically and write it rather than waiting for a library field that may not refresh.
candidates.trigger: A state property (e.g. `current_option`, `is_on`) reads one library attribute (`last_state`) while `async_select_option`/`async_turn_*` sets a different one (`state`), with no `async_write_ha_state` of the new value.

candidates.rule: Do not zero or clear brightness (or other level attributes) in a light's `async_turn_off`; leave the last level intact so it can be restored on the next turn-on.
candidates.trigger: `async_turn_off` in a light platform sets `self._attr_brightness = 0` or otherwise resets a level attribute.

candidates.rule: `_handle_coordinator_update` must refresh every entity attribute derived from coordinator data, including the entity name, not just a subset.
candidates.trigger: A `_handle_coordinator_update` override assigns some `_attr_*` values from the coordinator payload while other displayed attributes derived from the same payload are left untouched.

candidates.rule: Do not add per-update lookups that can only ever apply to a subset of devices; gate them behind a setup-time check or cached reference so unaffected devices pay nothing on each update.
candidates.trigger: An `available`/update path calls a topology lookup such as `node.get_compose_parent(...)` plus an attribute read on every invocation, unconditionally.

candidates.rule: Make availability precedence explicit when combining a bridged/composed parent's Reachable with the child endpoint's own: return the parent's verdict directly instead of falling through to the child's attribute.
candidates.trigger: An `available` property checks a parent endpoint's `Reachable` attribute and then continues on to read the child endpoint's `Reachable` when the parent is reachable.

candidates.rule: When deserializing stored KNX telegram values, accept every payload type the DPT layer can produce (str for DPT 16, dict for DPTComplex) rather than narrowing to numeric/bool types.
candidates.trigger: A restore/serialization path filters telegram payloads with `isinstance(value, (int, float, bool))` or a similarly narrow type check.

candidates.rule: A change that reroutes an existing device/event action to a new action type must be called out as a behavioral change in the PR description and release notes, even when it is the intended bug fix.
candidates.trigger: A diff adds a branch that maps a previously unhandled event type to a new action constant, changing which action existing automations receive.

candidates.rule: When an entity description's `key` is renamed, update the matching `translation_key` and its `strings.json` entries, or document in a comment why the old translation key is deliberately kept.
candidates.trigger: A diff changes the `key=` of an entity description but leaves the adjacent `translation_key=` unchanged.

candidates.rule: Reuse the shared `[%key:common::config_flow::data::*%]` translation references for standard config-flow fields (host, password, ssl, username, port) instead of introducing new literal labels.
candidates.trigger: A new or edited `strings.json` config_flow `data` block gives a plain string label for a field that already exists under `common::config_flow::data`.

candidates.rule: Every third-party module an integration imports must be declared in that integration's `manifest.json` requirements; do not swap an import to a differently named distribution without updating requirements.
candidates.trigger: A diff changes or adds a top-level import of a non-stdlib, non-homeassistant module in `homeassistant/components/<domain>/` without a corresponding `manifest.json` requirements change.

candidates.rule: A legacy YAML platform reduced to an import/repair-issue stub must still report successful setup - return a no-op service or `True` rather than `None` - so the legacy platform helper does not log a setup failure.
candidates.trigger: `async_get_service`, `async_get_scanner` or a comparable legacy platform entry point is rewritten to only create an issue/start an import flow and then return `None`.

candidates.rule: Handle the import flow's abort reasons before raising the `deprecated_yaml` repair issue, so a failed import does not tell the user their YAML was successfully migrated.
candidates.trigger: A YAML import path calls `async_create_issue(..., translation_key="deprecated_yaml")` unconditionally after starting an import flow, without branching on the flow's abort reason.

candidates.rule: Do not abort a reconfigure flow on unique-id mismatch when the existing entry still carries the integration's legacy unique_id; match the legacy value and migrate the entry to the new scheme.
candidates.trigger: A config flow computes a new-style unique id, calls `async_set_unique_id(...)` and then `_abort_if_unique_id_mismatch()` in the `SOURCE_RECONFIGURE` branch, in a diff that changes how the unique id is derived.

candidates.rule: Never assign to a config flow's `VERSION` or `MINOR_VERSION` at runtime; they are class-level constants describing the entry schema, and migrations must be driven by `async_migrate_entry`.
candidates.trigger: A diff contains `self.VERSION = ...` or `self.MINOR_VERSION = ...` inside a config-flow step or handler body.

candidates.rule: Reserve the `async_`/`_async_` prefix for coroutine functions and callbacks that run on the event loop; rename synchronous helpers to a plain `_setup_*`-style name.
candidates.trigger: A diff adds a `def _async_foo(...)`/`def async_foo(...)` that is not `async def` and contains no `await`.

candidates.rule: Filesystem traversal in media_source search must stream lazily and stop at the result cap instead of materializing or sorting the whole tree.
candidates.trigger: A diff calls sorted(path.rglob("*")) or otherwise builds a complete list of filesystem entries before a result limit such as MAX_SEARCH_RESULTS is applied.

candidates.rule: Coordinators must read configuration values off the config entry they already receive (entry.data[CONF_*]) instead of accepting the same values as extra constructor parameters.
candidates.trigger: A DataUpdateCoordinator subclass __init__ takes values such as latitude, longitude or host as parameters while also being handed the ConfigEntry those values come from.

candidates.rule: Optional service and config values validated with cv.string must be tested with `is not None`, never for truthiness, because the empty string is accepted input.
candidates.trigger: A handler writes `if call.data.get(ATTR_X):` (or a bare truthiness check) for a key whose voluptuous schema is cv.string.

candidates.rule: Entity capability flags must be set through the _attr_supported_features class attribute (or assigned in __init__), not returned from a @property.
candidates.trigger: A platform entity defines `@property def supported_features(self) -> ...Feature:` returning a constant flag combination.

candidates.rule: Code comments must describe the code as it stands; the reason a change was made belongs in the pull request, not in a comment left behind in the source.
candidates.trigger: A diff adds a comment that narrates the edit itself, e.g. explaining what an older dependency version used to render or why an existing value is being preserved.

candidates.rule: Pull requests must fill in the `## Proposed change` section and tick a `## Type of change` box, particularly when the diff alters config-flow behaviour.
candidates.trigger: PR body leaves the template's Proposed change section empty or has no Type of change checkbox selected, while the diff changes user-visible setup behaviour.

candidates.rule: When a successful update no longer contains a measurement, clear the cached native value and restore availability before writing state, so the entity reports unknown instead of the previous reading.
candidates.trigger: An update callback calls async_write_ha_state() on a branch that returns early because a value is missing, without resetting _attr_native_value or _attr_available first.

candidates.rule: Once an integration defines a `type XConfigEntry = ConfigEntry[RuntimeData]` alias, every function that takes that entry must be annotated with the alias rather than plain ConfigEntry.
candidates.trigger: A diff introduces a ConfigEntry type alias but leaves async_setup_entry/async_unload_entry or helper functions annotated with the bare ConfigEntry type.

candidates.rule: Entity state properties must tolerate missing upstream data and return None instead of raising; returning False from `available` does not stop Home Assistant from reading them.
candidates.trigger: A native_value, entity_picture or similar property indexes into a list, or looks a device up by id, with no guard for the entry being absent or removed.

candidates.rule: Diagnostics output must redact an identifier everywhere it can appear, including nested structures such as override target ids, not only in the collection that primarily lists it.
candidates.trigger: A diagnostics payload wraps one collection in async_redact_data but returns a sibling structure verbatim that can echo the same serials or ids.

candidates.rule: Timing behaviour introduced by a fix must be covered by a test that patches the module's asyncio.sleep and asserts the delay, not only by tests counting calls.
candidates.trigger: A diff adds an inter-command delay, pause or retry backoff while the accompanying tests only assert how many commands were sent.

candidates.rule: Coordinator subclasses must not re-annotate the inherited config_entry attribute; pass config_entry=None to super().__init__ and leave the base class type intact.
candidates.trigger: A DataUpdateCoordinator subclass body declares `config_entry: None` or otherwise narrows the annotation of config_entry.

candidates.rule: Library calls added to a coordinator's periodic update path must handle transient errors the same way the sibling calls around them do, so one failed poll does not propagate out of _async_update_data.
candidates.trigger: A new device/API command is added inside a coordinator method that runs every update interval, without the error suppression (e.g. suppress_errors=True) that the adjacent calls use.

candidates.rule: Service helpers that resolve a config entry from a device id must confirm the entry is loaded before touching runtime_data, raising ServiceValidationError rather than letting AttributeError escape.
candidates.trigger: Code calls hass.config_entries.async_get_entry(entry_id) inside a service call path and reads entry.runtime_data without checking the entry's loaded state.

candidates.rule: Value callables declared on custom EntityDescription subclasses must be typed with StateType (extended with datetime where needed) rather than a hand-narrowed return union.
candidates.trigger: A SensorEntityDescription/EntityDescription subclass declares a value or value_fn field typed as Callable[..., str | float | None] or another partial state union.

candidates.rule: Every translation key added to strings.json must be referenced by the integration's code, and every new error key must actually be raised on some code path; unreferenced keys have to be removed.
candidates.trigger: A diff adds exception or error keys to strings.json while no code in the same integration raises them via translation_key, or adds a raise path guarded by a condition nothing can reach.

candidates.rule: A new integration's initial quality_scale.yaml must already list the silver, gold and platinum rules, not just the bronze tier.
candidates.trigger: A newly added quality_scale.yaml contains only bronze-tier rule entries.

candidates.rule: MQTT command templates must be rendered with the same object that is supplied as the `value` template variable; do not pass a pre-serialized payload alongside the raw variables.
candidates.trigger: A call through MqttCommandTemplate/async_render passes json_dumps(x) as the payload while also supplying {"value": x} as template variables.

candidates.rule: Config-flow steps must not add a separate connectivity probe when an API call already made in that step proves the service is reachable and the user's selection is valid.
candidates.trigger: A config flow step adds an _async_test_connection()-style call after another call in the same step already queried the same API to validate user input.

candidates.rule: Entities that expose technical or diagnostic data must set _attr_entity_category = EntityCategory.DIAGNOSTIC, satisfying the entity-category quality-scale rule.
candidates.trigger: A new entity carrying technical information (feed status, last update time, upstream ids) is added with no entity_category, while the integration's quality_scale.yaml still lists entity-category as todo.

candidates.rule: Service parameters that require a newer backend must check the connected server's schema_version and raise the translated ServiceValidationError before the parameter is used.
candidates.trigger: A service handler reads a newly added parameter and forwards it to the library without an explicit version guard on server_info.schema_version or an equivalent capability field.

candidates.rule: When a service option lets the user pick a combination of values, expose it as a `select` selector with `multiple: true` rather than inventing a synthetic combined option such as `both`, matching the selector shape sibling integrations already use for the same service.
candidates.trigger: A `services.yaml` diff adds or edits a `select` selector whose `options` list contains an aggregate value (`both`, `all`, `any`) alongside the individual values.

candidates.rule: Exception and issue messages in `strings.json` that reuse text defined elsewhere must point at it with an exact `[%key:component::<domain>::<section>::<key>%]` reference, with no stray whitespace inside the reference path.
candidates.trigger: A `strings.json` diff adds a message whose value is a `[%key:...%]` reference, or duplicates a message string already defined under `config`/`exceptions` in the same file.

candidates.rule: `quality_scale.yaml` exemption comments must not contradict `manifest.json`; if a rule is marked exempt because the integration "does not poll", the manifest `iot_class` must agree (or the comment must state precisely what it does instead).
candidates.trigger: A PR adds or edits `quality_scale.yaml` entries with `status: exempt` and a justification comment about polling, actions, or discovery that conflicts with the integration's `manifest.json`.

candidates.rule: Import a library's exception classes from one module path consistently across the integration and its tests, and confirm that path is actually exported by the version pinned in `manifest.json`.
candidates.trigger: A PR bumps a library and adds imports of its exception types, with the integration importing from the package root while the tests import the same names from a submodule (or vice versa).

candidates.rule: A `deprecated_yaml` repair issue description must name the concrete legacy action/service names the user actually has (e.g. `tts.picotts_say`), not a templated glob like `tts.{domain}_*_say`.
candidates.trigger: `strings.json` adds an `issues.deprecated_yaml` description that refers to the services being removed with a wildcard or placeholder pattern.

candidates.rule: A dependency-bump PR must contain only the changes required by the version update; new user-facing entities, platforms, or features belong in a separate feature PR.
candidates.trigger: A PR whose stated purpose is bumping a library version also adds entity descriptions, dispatch entries, constants, fixtures, and tests for a new entity.

candidates.rule: When an integration runs more than one `DataUpdateCoordinator`, give each a distinct `name` (e.g. `f"{DOMAIN}_{self.__class__.__name__}"`) rather than passing `DOMAIN` to all of them.
candidates.trigger: `coordinator.py` adds a second coordinator subclass whose `super().__init__()` passes the same `name=DOMAIN` as the existing coordinator.

candidates.rule: A coordinator that fans out over several devices/endpoints must fetch them concurrently (`asyncio.gather(..., return_exceptions=True)`) and isolate per-item failures, keeping previous values for the ones that error instead of failing the whole refresh.
candidates.trigger: `_async_update_data` awaits an API call inside a `for` loop over endpoints/devices, letting the first exception abort the whole update.

candidates.rule: Name a module-level tuple of `EntityDescription` objects after the platform it populates (`SENSOR_DESCRIPTIONS`, `SELECT_TYPES`), not after one entity or one subset of the entities it contains.
candidates.trigger: A platform module (`sensor.py`, `select.py`, ...) declares a `tuple[...EntityDescription, ...]` constant, or a diff adds descriptions to an existing one so the constant now covers more than its name implies.

candidates.rule: Diagnostics collectors must only read known-safe attributes of the device/client object and must never invoke callables found on it.
candidates.trigger: `diagnostics.py` walks attributes of a client/device object and calls anything it finds callable (`if callable(val): val = val()`), or uses `hasattr()` followed by `getattr()` to probe for attributes.

candidates.rule: Build the diagnostics payload by dumping the coordinator/client data directly into a dict; do not add a generic recursive JSON-coercion layer that walks arbitrary object graphs.
candidates.trigger: `diagnostics.py` adds a helper that recursively coerces arbitrary values (lists/dicts/sets/enums/callables) into JSON-safe values, with depth limits or type fallbacks.

candidates.rule: Production integration code must not detect or branch on test doubles; fix the fixture or the test instead of adding mock-aware code paths under `homeassistant/components/`.
candidates.trigger: A file under `homeassistant/components/` references `mock_add_spec`, `unittest.mock`, `MagicMock`, or otherwise special-cases behaviour when the object appears to be a mock.

candidates.rule: Diagnostics output must be deterministic: never emit values rendered through a default `repr`/`str` that embeds memory addresses or other run-specific detail; use a stable representation such as the type name or `__qualname__`.
candidates.trigger: `diagnostics.py` formats an unknown object into the payload via an f-string or `str()` fallback (`f"<{type(k).__name__}: {k}>"`) for keys or values of arbitrary type.

candidates.rule: During `async_setup_entry`, configure the library client so connection and auth exceptions propagate instead of being swallowed by a client-side "suppress errors" mode, so setup can raise `ConfigEntryNotReady`/auth failure; keep the suppressing mode for the post-setup refresh loop only.
candidates.trigger: `__init__.py` constructs the integration's API client for setup with a flag (e.g. `initial=True`) that suppresses or only logs exceptions, then wraps the first call in try/except.

candidates.rule: A workaround that overrides entity `available` (or any other device-quirk fallback) must ship a regression test covering both the workaround path and the genuine-failure path, asserting real unavailable events still mark the entity unavailable.
candidates.trigger: `entity.py` overrides the `available` property with device- or API-type-specific special casing (e.g. only for `APIType.LOCAL`) and the PR adds no matching test.

candidates.rule: Config-flow credential validation that iterates a listing endpoint must treat an empty result as a validation failure (set `errors["base"]`) rather than creating the entry, and `async_setup_entry` must apply the same check.
candidates.trigger: `config_flow.py` validates the connection by iterating an API listing (`async for _ in client.models.list(): break`) and only treats raised exceptions as failure.

candidates.rule: Entity platform turn-on methods must apply every optional kwarg the platform contract passes them (e.g. fan async_turn_on must apply percentage and preset_mode) rather than accepting and discarding them.
candidates.trigger: A platform entity method signature declares optional service kwargs such as percentage, preset_mode, brightness or transition, but the body never reads them.

candidates.rule: YAML configuration schemas must constrain enumerated options with vol.In over the known constants and normalize case with vol.Lower instead of accepting free-form cv.string when downstream code branches on specific values.
candidates.trigger: A voluptuous CONFIG_SCHEMA entry uses cv.string for a key whose value is later compared against named constants or treated specially by import/setup logic.

candidates.rule: Entity unique_id and DeviceInfo identifiers must include the parent object's identifier whenever a child resource name is only unique within its parent, so two parents exposing the same name do not collide.
candidates.trigger: A unique_id or DeviceInfo identifiers f-string is built from the config entry id plus a resource name, for a resource enumerated per node/hub/bridge rather than globally.

candidates.rule: Numeric sensor entity descriptions must declare a state_class consistent with the integration's sibling sensors of the same device_class so the sensor participates in long-term statistics.
candidates.trigger: A new SensorEntityDescription sets device_class and native_unit_of_measurement for a numeric value but omits state_class, while neighbouring descriptions in the same tuple set one.

candidates.rule: Uptime and other duration-since-boot sensors must not use SensorStateClass.MEASUREMENT; omit state_class or use TOTAL, matching how existing core integrations model uptime.
candidates.trigger: A SensorEntityDescription combines SensorDeviceClass.DURATION or an uptime translation_key with state_class=SensorStateClass.MEASUREMENT.

candidates.rule: Raw unit strings taken from a device or API payload must be normalized and validated against Home Assistant's canonical units for the entity's device_class, falling back to the entity description's default when unrecognized, before being assigned to native_unit_of_measurement.
candidates.trigger: A payload or MQTT property value is assigned directly to self._attr_native_unit_of_measurement without mapping it through the canonical unit constants.

candidates.rule: An EntityDescription must keep a single source of truth for the callable that produces an entity's value; do not add a factory field alongside a mandatory value_fn that it overrides.
candidates.trigger: A description dataclass gains an optional *_factory callable while the original mandatory callable field stays required, and the entity picks one at runtime.

candidates.rule: When entity creation becomes conditional on optional payload keys, add a regression test using the reduced payload that asserts only the always-available entities are created and no KeyError occurs.
candidates.trigger: A platform's async_setup_entry gains `if "<key>" in data` guards around entity creation without a matching test fixture that omits those keys.

candidates.rule: When value helpers return None so an entity reports `unknown` instead of becoming unavailable, add tests feeding payloads with the missing or None fields to prove the helpers return None without raising and the update does not crash.
candidates.trigger: New value_fn helpers introduce `return None` paths for absent payload fields, with tests covering only fully-populated and idle payloads.

candidates.rule: A pull request must add only the entities and behaviour its title and description announce; extra platform entities must be removed or the PR description updated to cover them.
candidates.trigger: A platform module gains an additional entity description beyond the single feature named in the PR title/body.

candidates.rule: Do not commit developer-machine artefacts into an integration directory: local AI-assistant instruction files and absolute paths under a contributor's home directory must be removed or replaced with generic placeholders.
candidates.trigger: A new integration adds files such as CLAUDE.md, or any committed file containing absolute paths like /Users/<name>/ or C:\Users\<name>\.

candidates.rule: Integration code may only call library APIs that exist in the exact version pinned in manifest.json requirements; bump the pinned requirement in the same PR when the code depends on a newer attribute or method.
candidates.trigger: A diff uses a client attribute or method while manifest.json requirements pin a version of that library that does not provide it.

candidates.rule: Changes to config entry migration or import logic must ship migration tests covering the exact value shapes whose handling changed, including every stored location the value can come from.
candidates.trigger: A diff modifies async_migrate_entry, an import step, or normalization of stored config entry data, without adding test cases for the newly-handled input variants.

candidates.rule: When service registration is moved into services.py, __init__.py must import async_setup_services and call it from an async_setup, and define CONFIG_SCHEMA = cv.config_entry_only_config_schema(DOMAIN).
candidates.trigger: A refactor adds services.py with async_setup_services while __init__.py loses its registration code and gains no async_setup that calls it.

candidates.rule: Platform entity classes must reuse the data attributes already stored by the integration's shared base entity in entity.py instead of re-assigning their own copy of the same object.
candidates.trigger: A platform module's __init__ assigns self.<something> to a constructor argument that it also passes to super().__init__, where the base entity in entity.py already stores it.

candidates.rule: EntityDescription subclasses must be named for the object they describe followed by the platform, matching the naming already used by the integration's other platform modules.
candidates.trigger: A new @dataclass EntityDescription subclass is added in a platform module with a name whose object/platform word order differs from the equivalent classes in the integration's sibling platforms.

candidates.rule: Config flow error translation must map only 4xx API failures to specific user-facing error keys; server-side (5xx) failures must be reported the same way the runtime setup path reports them.
candidates.trigger: A config_flow except branch converts a broad API exception into a specific abort/error key without inspecting the HTTP status code, while coordinator.py distinguishes client from server errors on the same endpoint.

candidates.rule: Trigger async_start_reauth only for authentication failures (401); authorization or permission failures (403) must raise ConfigEntryError instead, since re-entering credentials cannot fix them.
candidates.trigger: A setup or coordinator except branch calls config_entry.async_start_reauth for any 4xx status, or for a generic API exception, without isolating 401.

candidates.rule: When a translated setup error interpolates an exception into translation_placeholders, the placeholder must carry the original library exception's detail (its message or __cause__), never the repr of a bare wrapper exception.
candidates.trigger: A ConfigEntryNotReady/ConfigEntryError raised with translation_placeholders formats an exception that was itself raised bare with `raise CustomError from err`.

candidates.rule: Dynamic entity add/remove logic must not treat a temporarily offline or unreachable device as removed; keep its last-known children or exclude it from the pruning step so entities are not re-added when it returns.
candidates.trigger: A coordinator update returns empty collections for a device based on an offline/unavailable status, and those collections feed a known-set intersection that drives async_add_entities.

candidates.rule: Changes to DeviceInfo fields such as configuration_url must be covered by snapshot tests of the device and entity registry for every device type the integration creates.
candidates.trigger: A diff adds or edits DeviceInfo attributes in an integration's entity.py without touching the snapshot tests or ambr snapshot files.

candidates.rule: When calling public hassio/supervisor helpers such as get_os_info, catch HassioNotReadyError and re-raise it as PlatformNotReady (with translation_domain and translation_key) instead of treating a None return as the failure fallback.
candidates.trigger: Platform setup calls a hassio helper (get_os_info, get_host_info, ...) and guards the result with `if x is None` or `None if x is None else ...` rather than catching HassioNotReadyError.

candidates.rule: When a platform only creates entities for keys that happen to be present in coordinator.data at setup time, add a coordinator listener that creates those entities later when the data first appears.
candidates.trigger: async_setup_entry builds entities inside `if <key> in coordinator.data` (or iterates an optional sub-structure) with no coordinator.async_add_listener registered to add entities on later refreshes.

candidates.rule: Values passed in translation_placeholders must be deterministically formatted user-facing strings; never interpolate a raw Python container repr such as str(set) or str(dict).
candidates.trigger: A HomeAssistantError/ServiceValidationError raise builds translation_placeholders from str() of a set, list, or dict.

candidates.rule: Config entry and subentry migrations must preserve any value the user already has, defaulting a new option only when its key is absent.
candidates.trigger: async_migrate_entry / async_update_subentry writes `data={**entry.data, CONF_NEW: False}`, i.e. the new default is spread after the existing data and overwrites it.

candidates.rule: A change that alters behavior users may already depend on must be declared as a breaking change in the PR description.
candidates.trigger: A diff changes existing runtime behavior (initial coordinator data, default values, emitted states) in a PR whose description has no breaking-change section.

candidates.rule: Raise ConfigEntryError, ConfigEntryNotReady and similar user-facing exceptions with translation_domain and translation_key plus an `exceptions` entry in strings.json, not a hard-coded English message.
candidates.trigger: An integration raises ConfigEntryError/ConfigEntryAuthFailed/HomeAssistantError with a literal English string argument.

candidates.rule: Trigger, condition and action YAML target selectors must list every domain the feature applies to, including the matching input_* helper domain.
candidates.trigger: A triggers.yaml / conditions.yaml / services.yaml target entity selector names a single `domain:` where the corresponding helper domain (input_select, input_boolean, input_number, ...) also implements the behavior.

candidates.rule: Device-quirk workarounds must not be added to a core entity base class without an architecture proposal that pins down the exact semantics (thresholds, drift windows, behaviors).
candidates.trigger: A diff adds normalization/heuristic logic (e.g. _normalize_uptime with an implicit tolerance) to homeassistant/components/<domain>/__init__.py entity base classes.

candidates.rule: New entity service/command implementations (play_media, browse_media, and similar) need behavior tests that call them; a snapshot-only platform test is not sufficient coverage.
candidates.trigger: A platform gains async_play_media/async_browse_media/other command methods while tests/components/<domain>/ only contains snapshot assertions.

candidates.rule: Validate user-supplied service arguments before converting them and raise HomeAssistantError/ServiceValidationError; never let a raw ValueError or TypeError from a cast or library call reach the user.
candidates.trigger: An entity service method passes a user-provided value straight into int()/float()/enum lookup, or into a library call, without try/except translating the failure into a HA error.

candidates.rule: Do not report fabricated progress values from an update entity; omit in_progress/update_percentage when the device does not expose a real percentage.
candidates.trigger: An UpdateEntity property returns hard-coded percentages (e.g. 75 while installing, 25 otherwise) derived from a status enum rather than a device-reported number.

candidates.rule: Normalize MAC and Bluetooth addresses with homeassistant.helpers.device_registry.format_mac before putting them into device registry connections.
candidates.trigger: A device_info/connections set is built with a raw address or an ad-hoc `.lower()` for CONNECTION_NETWORK_MAC or CONNECTION_BLUETOOTH.

candidates.rule: Do not set the `name` field on an entity description that also has a translation_key; entity naming comes from strings.json.
candidates.trigger: An EntityDescription literal declares both `translation_key=` and `name=` (or declares `name=` in an integration whose strings.json carries entity names).

candidates.rule: Mappings derived from device capability data must be rebuilt when used or refreshed on update events, not computed once in __init__.
candidates.trigger: An entity caches a dict built from device status/capabilities in __init__ and a service method reads that cache with a slugify/raw fallback when the key is missing.

candidates.rule: Do not change the value of an existing entity state or state attribute (for example by slugifying it); keep the raw value and add a map from API keys to HA translation keys for display.
candidates.trigger: A diff wraps a previously exposed attribute value in slugify()/lower()/rename, changing what `attributes.<name>` reports for existing installs.

candidates.rule: Split a user-visible bug fix into its own minimal PR so it can be cherry-picked into a patch release, and land test fixtures or refactors in a follow-up.
candidates.trigger: A PR mixes a small behavioral bugfix with large fixture/snapshot additions in the same change.

candidates.rule: Every new enum state value exposed by an entity must ship a matching translation entry under the entity's `state` block in strings.json in the same PR.
candidates.trigger: A diff adds new device-class/enum state constants or `options` values to an entity without adding the corresponding keys to the integration's strings.json.

candidates.rule: Error and warning messages raised from integrations that can have multiple config entries or devices must identify the failing entry or device (title, host, entry_id, or device name).
candidates.trigger: A _LOGGER.warning/_LOGGER.error or UpdateFailed/ConfigEntryError message is a fixed string with no entry or device identifier, in a coordinator or callback that serves several entries/devices (e.g. gathering over `client.beds.values()`).

candidates.rule: Coordinator-based platforms must not set PARALLEL_UPDATES to a positive number; use 0 (or omit it) so CoordinatorEntity updates are not serialized.
candidates.trigger: A platform module whose entities derive from CoordinatorEntity adds `PARALLEL_UPDATES = 1` (or any value > 0).

candidates.rule: When adding an entity description whose value_fn can return None, extend the integration's mock fixture data so the entity is actually created, and regenerate the platform snapshot to cover it.
candidates.trigger: A new EntityDescription is added to a platform but tests/components/<domain>/ fixtures or mock_data.py contain no value for the key it reads, so the entity is skipped at setup.

candidates.rule: Do not rename existing translation keys in strings.json; keep the established key even when its name is inconsistent, because renaming discards all existing translations.
candidates.trigger: A strings.json diff removes an existing key and adds the same content under a different key name (renaming/reprefixing), rather than only adding new keys.

candidates.rule: Do not expose one translated enum state per vendor error code; collapse variants that are not individually actionable for the user into a single shared state.
candidates.trigger: A strings.json or enum diff adds many near-identical state values distinguished only by a device error number (e.g. drying_error, drying_error_e_12, drying_error_e_13).

candidates.rule: Register push-update listeners in async_added_to_hass unconditionally via async_on_remove; do not hasattr-guard the listener API to paper over an imprecise attribute type.
candidates.trigger: async_added_to_hass wraps `add_update_listener` (or similar subscription call) in `if hasattr(self._trait, ...)` while sibling platforms in the same integration register it unconditionally.
